capabilities: Render .html and .htm files in a dedicated view from the file explorer, command palette, or context menu
Run page scripts and styles so self-contained pages like forms, dashboards and reports work as written
Inject a <base href> so relative images, CSS and JS next to the file keep resolving
Reload, open the file in the system browser, or copy its path from a toolbar
Configure sandbox safety switches, including allow-same-origin and backdrop-filter handling
extras: The manifest carries the warning that the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README warns that previews run the page's own JavaScript and only trusted HTML should be opened.
problem: Obsidian treats HTML files as plain text, so reading a local HTML page means leaving the app or opening a browser.
summary: HTML file viewer that renders local .html and .htm files in a dedicated Obsidian view with their styles and scripts running.
